note: NY-close read, Tue 2026-11-24 (~3:00 PM CT; levels are the latest verified reads into the close, as of ~11:30 AM-1:00 PM CT — search-based reads lag the 3:00 PM CT fix). Turnaround Tuesday: the dollar gives back Monday's 19-month-high surge — DXY 103.85 (-0.34%) as yields ease (10Y 4.89%, lowest since Nov 10) and equities fade after Monday's Nvidia relief rally; the reported plan for new Section 301 duties on 16 economies (findings expected Tue/Wed, not yet released) weighs on risk. EUR/USD 1.0972 and GBP/USD 1.3117 reclaim ~0.7% each off 19-month / 1-year lows; Greene hawkish (disinflation stalled) and Macklem hawkish-leaning (Dec 9 odds jump to ~80%) add to the bid. USD/JPY 159.27 pinned below 160. Confidence smashed it: 103.3 vs 92.1 fcst, highest since Jan 2025 — but the dollar didn't reclaim the day's losses. Oil rebounds: Brent $90.65 / WTI $81.49 after the second Houthi strike on Riyadh's PIF Tower (11 hurt) — the tape still trades surplus vs Gulf risk. Gold fades to ~$3,556 (-2.4%) off Monday's rebound. Tonight: AU CPI 6:30 PM CT (fcst 4.7% y/y). Wednesday's 7:30 AM CT cluster (core PCE, Q3 GDP 2nd estimate, claims) plus the Beige Book is the week's big data day; US markets closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. Spot levels are indicative index quotes, not executable prices.
